clauses.reason: Operative as amended. Section 4 provides for the Legion of Merit: paragraph (a) lets the Secretaries award it, without degree, to a member of the Armed Forces who after September 8, 1939 has distinguished himself or herself by exceptionally meritorious conduct in performing outstanding services; paragraph (b) lets the Secretary of Defense, after concurrence by the Secretary of State, award it in degrees to members of friendly foreign armed forces; paragraph (c) has the Secretary of Defense submit Chief Commander recommendations to the President. EO 14085 section 5(e) changed any member to members and the singular distinguished-himself-or-herself wording to the plural in paragraph (a) and struck the word his in paragraph (c); the awards continue.

clauses.reason: Operative as amended. Section 5 provides for the Distinguished Flying Cross: (a) award authority for heroism or extraordinary achievement in aerial flight aboard an aircraft or spacecraft, (b) eligibility of members of the Armed Forces and of friendly foreign forces serving with them and not of civilians, (c) a bar on award where later service was not honorable, (d) time limits on award by period of the qualifying act (before July 2, 1926; December 7, 1941 to September 2, 1945; September 3, 1945 to December 31, 1946; July 2, 1926 to September 10, 2001; on or after September 11, 2001), (e) posthumous award and (f) one cross per person with bars. EO 14085 section 5(f) replaced any eligible person with eligible persons and the singular verb with the plural in section 5(a); the time limits in (d) are limits on awards and remain part of the text.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register original (83 FR 18191, PDF pages 1-4) is Executive Order 13830 of April 20, 2018, Delegation of Authority To Approve Certain Military Decorations, signed by Donald J. Trump. Its sections 1 to 6 promulgate the award rules for twelve decorations, section 7 gives regulation authority and section 8 contains general provisions including the supersession of Executive Orders 4601 and 9260. The packet inventory did not match the text (it contained duplicated sub-items such as sec5-b-dup2 and sec5-i-ii); it is corrected by overrides to eleven section-level clauses. EO 14085 section 5 (October 3, 2022) amended the paragraph before section 1 and sections 1 to 6 by striking and inserting words (statutory section numbers, those individuals, Space Force, plural verbs); sections 7 and 8 were not amended. Current law: the held U.S. Code note under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57 prints the order as amended by EO 14085 section 5 with no ending (release point 119-121, through 2026-10-09). No instrument revokes it.

All remain in force as amended."}
